newsitem.title: USA: EIA revises down U.S. natgas demand for 1997.
newsitem.headline: EIA revises down U.S. natgas demand for 1997.

text.p: U.S. natural gas demand is expected to grow 1.2 percent in 1997 to 22.25 trillion cubic feet, the Energy Information Administration said Thursday, revising down an earlier forecast of a 1.4 percent rise.
The lower growth outlook reflected the mild weather this winter and high prices at the beginning of the year, the agency said in its latest short-term energy outlook.

While lowering its 1997 outlook, it hiked its forecast for 1998, seeing growth surging by 4.4 percent to 23.23 Tcf with a drop in prices and hydropower output, compared with an earlier projection of 2.3 percent growth to 23.1 Tcf.

Natural gas prices are now expected to average $2.24 per thousand cubic feet in 1997, off one cent from last year's average, but up 15 cents from EIA's earlier projection for 1997 based on lofty prices at the beginning of the year.
The agency said natural gas demand in 1996 ended up lower than expected at only 21.99 Tcf because soaring prices prompted power plants to switch to other fuels.
Industrial demand, the largest sector for natural gas, is expected to climb 2.6 percent in 1997 and 1998 to 8.82 Tcf this year and 9.05 Tcf next year.
Utility demand for natural gas is projected to jump 13 percent in 1997 to 3.1 Tcf, and rise by another 12.6 percent in 1998 to 3.49 Tcf.

At the same time, residential demand is expected to fall five percent to 4.96 Tcf in 1997, but climb 3.7 percent in 1998, assuming weather conditions are more normal next year and more homes use natural gas heating.
EIA lowered its outlook for annual U.S. dry gas production in 1997 to 19.19 Tcf from an earlier forecast of 19.43 Tcf, but that was still up from 19.02 Tcf in 1996.
Net gas imports are still expected to be around 2.9 Tcf in 1997 and 3.19 Tcf in 1998, up from 2.69 Tcf last year.
